root_idea.summary: The root denotes cutting off something before its completion, with extensions to severed continuation, relationship, benefit, or posterity.
root_idea.development: The physical notion of cutting before completion develops into descriptions of tails or objects being severed, ties of kinship being broken, good or prosperity being cut off, and a person lacking offspring or enduring remembrance. The Quranic epithet specializes this idea in the severing of lasting mention.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quranic nominal epithet under its normalized masculine singular citation form.

senses.definition: One cut off from lasting mention or legacy; the one whose enduring remembrance is severed.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic epithet, the severance concerns enduring ذكر (mention). The interpretation relates this to the supposed loss of posterity, but the stated Quranic meaning is the severing of lasting remembrance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or cut off something before its completion; to amputate a tail wholly or at any point.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the object may be a thing generally, with the tail given as a prominent application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sever the ties of kinship and disassociate oneself from one's relations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with kinship or relationship ties as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to be without offspring or progeny.
To become cut off, wholly or partly, as a tail or similar object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VII intransitive or middle construction describing the resulting state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cutting or sharp sword; by extension, an intensely sharp implement or instrument.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal epithet for a sword or other cutting implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the tail wholly or partly cut off; a tailless or short-tailed beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival description of an animal whose tail has been amputated or is deficient.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short-tailed or otherwise specified noxious serpent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological use, including the serpent described as having a short tail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather water-bag or bucket lacking its loop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a container considered incomplete because its loop is absent.
Figurative adjectival use associated with deficiency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Suffering loss or being a loser.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use synonymous with being in a state of loss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or thing cut off from good or prosperity, or whose beneficial effect has been cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use for deprivation of benefit or the cessation of a beneficial result.
An adjectival description of a person lacking descendants; distinct from the Quranic specialization in severed lasting mention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sermon or formal address that omits the praise of God and the blessing of the Prophet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for an address regarded as incomplete in its opening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single prayer-unit performed instead of a complete two-unit performance, or a prayer-unit cut short after one unit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional ritual expression for an incomplete or truncated performance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The ass and the slave, called “the two abtars” because of the little good attributed to them.
Short or abbreviated, as though cut off before completion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use emphasizing curtailed length or incompletion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who severs the ties of kinship, or who is quick to sever the bond between himself and a friend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive personal epithet for one who habitually cuts relational ties.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Having a tail cut off is covered by the cutting branch.
Form IV causative use concerning offspring.
Abtar as having the tail cut off.
Partial or complete tail amputation is covered by the tail meaning.
Water-bag or bucket without a loop.
A person deprived of good or prosperity.
A thing whose beneficial effect is cut off.
Fixed expression for the ass and the slave.
Intensive epithet for severing relational ties.

cautions: The Quranic use in 108:3 concerns severed enduring mention; the broader Classical Arabic sense “without offspring” is listed separately and should not be treated as the complete Quranic definition.
